prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” roofer for hail damage in Denver — the right contractor depends on your exact location, the size/type of the job (residential vs. commercial), your insurance situation, and what warranties/certifications you want. I can help you find the best fit. To get started, tell me your ZIP code and whether this is a home or a commercial property.

Meanwhile, here’s how to identify the best hail-damage roofer in Denver and what to look for:

What to look for
- Hail/storm damage experience: Ask how many hail repairs they’ve handled and for local references from recent storm seasons.
- Insurance-claims expertise: Prefer contractors who work regularly with insurers and can provide an Xactimate-style estimate.
- Manufacturer certifications: Look for GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Platinum, etc. These mean access to better warranties.
- License and insurance: Verify business registration, general liability insurance, and workers’ compensation. Check city/county requirements.
- Written estimates & scope: Get a detailed, line-item estimate with materials, tear-off vs. overlay, and timeline.
- Warranties: Ask about workmanship/installation warranties and confirmation that material manufacturers’ warranties are transferrable if you sell the house.
- Local reputation: Check Google Reviews, BBB, Yelp, and ask neighbors; get at least 3 bids.
- No-pressure, transparent process: Avoid roofers with high-pressure sales tactics or who ask for large upfront sums beyond reasonable deposits.

Red flags / avoid
- Storm-chasers (out-of-area companies who show up after a storm) — can be legitimate but need extra vetting.
- “Sign over your insurance check” requests without clear written terms.
- Vague contracts, no business address, or no proof of insurance.
- Extremely low bids that don’t itemize materials or labor.

Questions to ask a roofer
- How many local hail jobs have you completed in the last 12 months?
- Are you licensed/registered here in Colorado and insured (GL and WC)? Can you provide certificates?
- Which shingle brands do you install and what certifications do you have?
- Will you handle insurance communication/estimates? Do you charge for this?
- What’s included in the warranty? Is it written?
- Can you provide recent local references and photos of completed hail repairs?

If you want, I can:
- Pull a short list of highly rated hail-repair roofers near your ZIP code,
- Outline typical pricing ranges for your roof size/material,
- Or walk you through filing an insurance claim and the inspection process.

Tell me your ZIP code and whether it’s a residential or commercial roof and I’ll find nearby, well-reviewed options.
